coastal_data.CD_altimetry.combine_openadb_nc_files(path)¶

Combines all netCDF files in all subfolders under ‘path’ into one .nc-file. Additionally, tweaks variable names and datetimes for further usage.

Parameters:

path (string) – parent folder (subfolders per mission and per pass)

Return type:

xarray Dataset

Returns:

Combined OpenADB NetCDF files

coastal_data.CD_altimetry.compute_ib_corr(path_input_general)¶

Compute inverse barometer correction. Downloads mean sea level pressure from ERA5 is not found in the specified path. :param path_input_general: Path to ERA5 data :type path_input_general: string :return: xxx :rtype: xxx

coastal_data.CD_altimetry.equalise_timeseries(ts1, ts2)¶

From two timeseries ts1 and ts2 with some overlap compute the bias from the overlap period as the mean of differences, and adjust ts1 so that both are on the average level of ts2.

Parameters:

  • ts1 (pandas Series with DateTime index) – Altimetry time series

  • ts2 (pandas Series with DateTime index) – Altimetry time series

Returns:

ts1 with bias to ts2 removed

Return type:

pandas Series

coastal_data.CD_altimetry.get_altimetry_timeseries_from_polygon(sla, lon, lat, time, epsg_in, epsg_out, poly, freq_average='ME')¶

If no tide gauge available, simply average all points inside a user-defined polygon.

Parameters:

  • sla (array-like (nx1)) – Sea level anomaly

  • lon (array-like (nx1)) – Longitude

  • lat (array-like (nx1)) – Latitude

  • time (array-like (nx1)) – Time

  • epsg_in (float) – CRS of the input data

  • epsg_out (float) – Desired crs of the output data (cannot be WGS84/epgs 4326). Cell numbers change for different output crs.

  • poly (shapely polygon) – Area over which to average all points, coordinates of the polygon must be the same crs as epsg_out

  • freq_average (string) – Period over which to average in pd.Grouper, (see https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/timeseries.html#offset-aliases)

Returns:

SLA, SSH and MSS of the created altimetry time series

Return type:

pandas DataFrame

coastal_data.CD_altimetry.get_altimetry_timeseries_with_TG(alt_data, labels, epsg_in, epsg_out, tg, tg_lon, tg_lat, gridsize, period_covered, freq_average='ME')¶

Create a timeseries from along-track altimetry data that fits best to a nearby tide gauge in terms of correlation, RMSE and trend difference.

The function presents maps and high-scores lists for each parameter, and asks the user to manually select the cells from which to extract the timeseries.

Parameters:

  • alt_data (xarray Dataset) – Altimetry data (e.g. output from clean_openadb_ales or clean_rads)

  • labels (dict) – Names of the variable in alt_data, e.g.: labels = {‘time’:’time’, ‘lon’:’glon’, ‘lat’:’glat’, ‘ssh’:’ssh’, ‘mssh’:’mssh’}

  • epsg_in (float) – CRS of the input data

  • epsg_out (float) – Desired crs of the output data (cannot be WGS84/epgs 4326). Cell numbers change for different output crs.

  • tg (pandas Series) – Corrected tide gauge data (corrected for IB and VLM), must include DatetimeIndex

  • tg_lon (float) – Longitude of tide gauge

  • tg_lat (float) – Latitude of tide gauge

  • gridsize (dict) – Gridsize in x- and y-direction to bin timeseries into chessboard-cells, e.g.: gridsize = {‘x’:25, ‘y’:25} # [km]

  • period_covered (dict) – Min and max dates of the timeseries used for comparison with the tide gauge, (to ensure that timeseries are long enough), e.g.: period_covered = {‘min’:’2002-07-01’, ‘max’:’2020-03-31’}

  • freq_average (string) – Period over which to average in pd.Grouper, (see https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/timeseries.html#offset-aliases)

Returns:

SLA, SSH and MSS for one time series per grid cell

Return type:

pandas DataFrame

coastal_data.CD_altimetry.reformat_chess_data(cell_stats, param, x_vec, y_vec)¶
This function does 2 things:

  1. Adding nans for the cells which don’t contain data

  2. Reshapes the values in a way that plotting with pcolormesh colors the right fields on the map.
